 UVA buys old State Farm center for hospital services expansion

 ALBEMARLE COUNTY, Va. (CBS19 NEWS) — The University of Virginia has purchased a building on Pantops that has sat mostly unused since 2020 as part of an effort to expand access to outpatient care.
 During a UVA Board of Visitors meeting on Friday, it was announced that the 365,000-square-foot State Farm operations center had been purchased for $37.7 million, after UVA Health received payments from the previous tenant for terminating their lease obligations early.
 UVA says the 55-acre property near Richmond Road and Interstate 64 will be a convenient location for patients to use.
 “The acquisition of this property is an investment in the health of the communities we serve,” said UVA President Scott Beardsley. “The new facility, once refurbished with the goal of opening in 2028, will enable the incredible UVA Health team to meet growing demand for its clinical expertise. Patient care and public service are central to the University of Virginia’s mission, and this is an important step for both.”
 According to a release, the purchase of this facility is one of the first major initiatives to come from UVA Health’s recently launched 10-year space planning initiative, “Expanding Care, Enhancing Lives,” which seeks to meet the steadily growing demand for both outpatient and inpatient care.
 UVA Health also plans to undergo a master planning process over the next six months that will determine which clinical service would be best served at the Pantops location, as well as the renovations that will be needed to accommodate clinic facilities.
 “With this new location on Pantops, combined with our University Medical Center outpatient locations at UVA Orthopedic Center Ivy Road, Northridge Medical Park, Fontaine Research Park and UVA Health Riverside in northern Albemarle County, our goal is to make it easier for patients to receive our high-quality care at convenient locations across the region,” said John Bennett, MPA, UVA Health’s chief service line and ambulatory officer.
 The release also says this purchase will help free up additional capacity at University Hospital to expand inpatient care.
 Work is already underway at the main hospital to accommodate more inpatients, with construction crews building out the top three floors of the South Tower to add beds to the NICU, pediatrics, and adult cancer care facilities.
 The release adds that planning is underway to repurpose the Transitional Care Hospital on Ivy Road into inpatient behavioral health rooms to free up even more beds at the main hospital.
 These projects are expected to add nearly 140 inpatient beds over the next three years.
 Finally, the health system is expanding laboratory services at North Fork Discovery Park, which will house lab services in a new and bigger location beginning in November 2027.
 State Farm stopped using the facility in 2020 when it shifted its employees to remote work during the COVID-19 pandemic.
